labels.label: supports
labels.note: The judge informed the defendant of his right to remain silent.
labels.observation: O1 (2025-06-02): The presiding judge informed Mr. Venn that he had the right to remain silent.

labels.label: supports
labels.note: The defendant chose to testify and did not face compulsion.
labels.observation: O2 (2025-06-02): Mr. Venn chose to make a statement, in which he denied the charge and said that his articles were based on documents given to him by employees of the Ministry of Water.

labels.label: unrelated
labels.note: The openness of the courtroom does not pertain to the right against self-incrimination.
labels.observation: O3 (2025-06-16): The courtroom was open to the public.

labels.label: unrelated
labels.note: The decision to exclude the public is related to national security, not the right against self-incrimination.
labels.observation: O4 (2025-06-30): At the prosecution's request, the presiding judge ordered the public and journalists to leave the courtroom during the testimony of a police investigator, citing national security.

labels.label: unrelated
labels.note: The request for witnesses is unrelated to the right against self-incrimination.
labels.observation: O5 (2025-06-30): Defence counsel asked the court to hear two witnesses, both editors at Mirevo Today, who had attended the editorial meeting at which the articles were approved.

labels.label: unrelated
labels.note: The refusal to hear witnesses is unrelated to the right against self-incrimination.
labels.observation: O6 (2025-06-30): The presiding judge refused to hear them, without giving reasons.

labels.label: unrelated
labels.note: The presence of the defence counsel is unrelated to the right against self-incrimination.
labels.observation: O7 (2025-07-14): Defence counsel Lena Brask was present and made the closing statement for the defence.

labels.label: unrelated
labels.note: The prosecutor's request for a sentence is unrelated to the right against self-incrimination.
labels.observation: O8 (2025-07-14): The prosecutor asked for a sentence of five years' imprisonment.
